injuries.summary:
### Key injury updates
- **Buccaneers CB Jacob Parrish** — **downgraded to OUT** for the rest of today’s game with a **back injury**.
- **Chargers QB Justin Herbert** — now in the **NFL concussion protocol** after the loss to the Jets. He **played the full game**, and it’s **unclear when the injury happened**.
- **Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith** — left the Eagles game with an apparent **left ankle injury** after a hot start. No final status update was provided.
- **49ers RT Colton McKivitz** — was **carted off** in Mexico City with a **lower-leg injury**.
- **Keaton Mitchell / David Njoku** — both suffered in-game injuries vs. the Jets:
  - **Mitchell**: **back injury**
  - **Njoku**: **shoulder setback**; he had **just returned from recent injuries**
- **Ravens RB Derrick Henry** — left for a **concussion evaluation** after his TD run, but **cleared concussion protocol** afterward.
- **Commanders defender** — picked up a **practice injury** ahead of Monday night vs. the Bengals, but the **player and injury were not specified**.

### Why it matters
- **Herbert** is the biggest fantasy and game-plan swing point here.
- **Highsmith** and **McKivitz** matter for pass rush and protection.
- **Parrish** being out weakens Tampa Bay’s secondary.
- **Njoku’s setback** is notable because he had just gotten back from injury.

### What to watch next
- Official follow-up on **Herbert’s concussion protocol** status.
- Any final update on **Highsmith, McKivitz, Mitchell, and Njoku**.
- The **Bengals-Commanders** injury report for the unnamed Washington defender.

PIT.summary:
- **Aaron Rodgers (QB)** — Pittsburgh’s offense was stuck in quick-game mode: the first four drives produced just 17 yards on 16 plays, and Rodgers averaged 0.5 air yards per attempt in the first half with 12 of 20 throws coming at or behind the line. That keeps his downfield projection capped and drags down the ceiling for the pass-catchers unless Mike McCarthy’s promised offensive adjustments materially change the plan. [11, 10]

- **DK Metcalf (WR)** — Metcalf’s Week 11 usage/output was a disaster: one catch for two yards before an ejection on multiple unsportsmanlike penalties. It doesn’t change his starting role, but it reinforces a volatile, low-floor weekly profile if Pittsburgh keeps funneling a short, disjointed passing game. [3, 9]

- **Spencer Anderson (LG)** — Mason McCormick’s absence has already pushed Anderson into the left guard spot, and the line struggled to create run push or keep Rodgers clean in the loss to Philadelphia. That lowers rushing efficiency for the backs and suppresses the whole offense’s fantasy ceiling this week. [6]

- **Alex Highsmith (OLB)** — Highsmith was seen in a walking boot after leaving with an ankle injury, and Pittsburgh is already thin on the edge with Nick Herbig out, leaving T.J. Watt, Jack Sawyer and K.J. Henry to carry the load. For PIT projections, this is mostly a Steelers DST/sack-upside note: the pass rush can still make plays, but the depth chart is shakier than usual. [4]

CIN.summary:
- **Chase Brown (RB)** — Cincinnati is still running a pass-first offense, and Brown’s role is built around that: he’s averaging just 12.6 carries per game, has more receptions than any RB in the league, and remains a trusted pass protector. For this week, his projection is more reception-driven than rushing-volume driven, so his floor is tied to game flow and checkdowns. [2, 4]

- **Ja’Marr Chase / Tee Higgins (WR)** — Higgins said both receivers can want the ball more, but Chase has moved ahead of him in receiving yards and touchdowns, underscoring how concentrated the target tree still is at the top. That keeps both in must-start territory, with Chase carrying the higher ceiling and Higgins still projecting for strong weekly volume. [12]

- **Joe Burrow / Bengals passing game** — Cincinnati has scored 30+ in five straight and owns the NFL’s top pass offense, while Washington has injuries piling up and has had trouble slowing offenses. That keeps Burrow, Chase, and Higgins at the center of Cincinnati’s weekly projection and supports a pass-heavy ceiling environment rather than a run-centric script. [5, 10, 4]

- **Cincinnati offensive line** — With Fairchild questionable and Risner out, the interior is a little thinner than usual, but this offense still has one of the league’s better pass-blocking setups. The impact is a modest pocket-stability downgrade for Burrow, not a major change in target distribution or the core skill-player outlook. [4, 6]
